title: "Teacher Safety Checklist"

## Pre-visit checklist

Before students enter the farm or work area, confirm that:

- [ ] the activity is appropriate for the age and capability of the students
- [ ] a safety briefing has been completed
- [ ] PPE is available and in good condition
- [ ] the work area has been checked for hazards
- [ ] the task has an identified supervisor
- [ ] emergency procedures and reporting steps are understood
- [ ] livestock, chemicals, or machinery are managed safely

## Daily farm risk checks

Use this during the lesson or work session:

- [ ] check the area for trips, uneven ground, or clutter
- [ ] confirm tools are safe and stored correctly
- [ ] check that students are wearing the correct PPE
- [ ] review the task procedure and work boundaries
- [ ] ensure students know the escape route around animals
- [ ] confirm chemicals are labelled, stored, and secured
- [ ] monitor student behaviour and communication throughout the task

## Activity-specific checks

### Animals

- [ ] animals have been approached calmly
- [ ] students know how to move around the animals safely
- [ ] there is a clear safe route away from the animal
- [ ] any injured or distressed animal is reported immediately

### Tools and equipment

- [ ] tools are suitable for the task
- [ ] sharp or damaged tools are removed from use
- [ ] tools are cleaned and stored correctly after use
- [ ] the area is left tidy and safe for the next group

### Chemicals

- [ ] chemical storage is secure and labelled
- [ ] PPE is available and used correctly
- [ ] spill kit is available and accessible
- [ ] chemicals are kept away from feed and water sources

## Incident response checklist

If an accident, injury, or near miss occurs:

- [ ] stop the task immediately
- [ ] ensure the area is safe
- [ ] provide first aid or contact the appropriate responder
- [ ] report the incident as required
- [ ] record what happened, who was involved, and what action was taken
- [ ] review the task and make changes to prevent recurrence
